newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam likely to consider new sites for refinery.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam likely to consider new sites for refinery.

text.p: Vietnam is likely to consider a proposal to build two oil refineries, one in the south and one in the north, instead of one large plant in the centre of the country, a government official said on Tuesday.

"Some people have already proposed not to build a 6.5-million-tonne (per year) refinery in central Vietnam, but a smaller one in the south and a second in the north," said Tran Quan Ngoc, the Ministry of Planning and Investment's General Director in charge of foreign investment in southern Vietnam.

"In our country there are different opinions on this," Ngoc told reporters on the sidelines of an oil, gas and petrochemicals conference. "And some scientists and economy experts are selling this idea to the government. I think our government will consider it."
Ngoc added he would like to see a refinery in the south, an area which accounts for 65 percent of the country's consumption, and said he hoped the government would change its mind on the location.
He said that under the new proposal, the combined capacity of the two refineries in the north and south of the country would be roughly equal to the planned 6.5 million tonnes a year at Dung Quat.

Vietnam's plans to build the $1.3 billion refinery at Dung Quat together with a foreign consortium broke up in acrimony earlier this year after state oil firm Petrovietnam rejected their demand for greater commercial and financial incentives.
